item.content:encoded:
Applications are now open for the Bloomberg Data Science Ph.D. Fellowship for the 2027–2028 academic year, an opportunity designed to support exceptional doctoral students conducting advanced research in data science, artificial intelligence, machine learning and related technical fields.

Bloomberg is inviting outstanding Ph.D. students working in relevant areas of study to apply for the fellowship. The program connects doctoral researchers with Bloomberg’s AI and machine learning research community, where researchers and engineers work on complex scientific and engineering challenges associated with Bloomberg technology and the Bloomberg Terminal.

The Bloomberg Data Science Ph.D. Fellowship provides a comprehensive package of financial and professional support. Selected fellows receive 100% tuition coverage, a USD 45,000 stipend, mentorship from Bloomberg professionals, career support and a paid 14-week research internship at Bloomberg. Fellows may also have an opportunity to renew their fellowship annually for up to three years, subject to Bloomberg’s discretion.

Applications, including all required documents and reference letters, must be submitted by Friday, September 25, 2026, at 11:59 PM Anywhere on Earth (AoE).

About the Bloomberg Data Science Ph.D. Fellowship

The Bloomberg Data Science Ph.D. Fellowship is an academic engagement initiative aimed at supporting Ph.D. candidates whose research can contribute to advances in data science, artificial intelligence, machine learning and other areas relevant to Bloomberg’s technology and research ecosystem.

The fellowship’s broader goal is to encourage doctoral researchers to produce meaningful research outputs. Bloomberg specifically highlights groundbreaking research publications, open-source contributions and other forms of research dissemination as outcomes that the fellowship is intended to encourage.

Rather than offering financial support alone, Bloomberg combines funding with professional and research development opportunities. Fellows receive mentorship, career counseling and access to research internships, creating opportunities to connect academic research with practical technical challenges.

Bloomberg has operated previous cohorts of its Data Science Ph.D. Fellowship, including cohorts for the 2018–2019 through 2024–2025 academic years.

Research Areas and Topics of Interest

Applicants should be pursuing doctoral research relevant to Bloomberg’s areas of interest.

For the current call, Bloomberg has identified a broad range of research topics. The list is not necessarily exhaustive, meaning applicants working in closely related fields may also have research that fits the program.

The stated topics of interest include:

  1. Agentic AI, Tool Use and Agent Infrastructure
    Research involving autonomous or semi-autonomous AI agents, the tools used by AI systems and the infrastructure required to develop and operate agent-based systems.
  2. Agent Evaluation and LLM Judges
    Research exploring methods for evaluating AI agents and the use, reliability and development of large language models as evaluators.
  3. Code Generation, Semantic Parsing and Text-to-API
    Work involving AI-assisted programming, translation of natural language into structured representations and systems that convert textual instructions into API interactions.
  4. Efficient Models, Distillation and Inference
    Research focused on improving the efficiency of machine learning models, model compression and distillation, and efficient inference techniques.
  5. Human-AI Collaboration, Data Annotation and Data-Centric AI
    Research examining how people and artificial intelligence systems interact, methods for improving data annotation and approaches that prioritize the quality and management of data used in AI development.
  6. Information Retrieval, RAG and Agentic Search
    Research covering information retrieval, retrieval-augmented generation and advanced AI-driven search systems.
  7. Information Synthesis, Summarization and Generation
    Work examining how AI systems can identify, combine, summarize and generate useful information from different sources.
  8. Knowledge Graphs, Structured and Neuro-symbolic Reasoning
    Research involving structured knowledge representations and systems that combine neural methods with symbolic reasoning.
  9. LLM Post-training, Domain Adaptation, Reasoning and Alignment
    Research exploring how large language models can be improved after initial training, adapted to particular domains, enhanced in their reasoning capabilities and aligned for intended uses.
  10. Multimodal Models and Document Intelligence
    Research involving models capable of processing multiple forms of information and technologies for understanding complex documents.
  11. Time-series Modeling, Forecasting and AI for Finance
    Research involving temporal data, predictive modeling, forecasting and applications of artificial intelligence within financial contexts.
  12. Trustworthy, Responsible and Secure AI
    Research addressing the reliability, responsibility, security and trustworthiness of artificial intelligence systems.

These research areas make the fellowship particularly relevant to doctoral researchers working at the intersection of computer science, data science, artificial intelligence, machine learning, natural language processing, information retrieval and related disciplines.

Bloomberg Data Science Ph.D. Fellowship Benefits

One of the major attractions of the Bloomberg Data Science Ph.D. Fellowship is its combination of academic funding and professional research experience.

Selected fellows will receive the following benefits:

1. 100% Tuition Coverage

Bloomberg states that the fellowship will cover 100% of the recipient’s tuition.

This provides substantial financial support for doctoral candidates during the fellowship period and allows selected researchers to focus more extensively on their academic and research responsibilities.

2. USD 45,000 Stipend

Each recipient will receive a USD 45,000 stipend.

Bloomberg states that the stipend can support:

  • Living expenses;
  • Attendance at professional conferences; and
  • Research-related expenses, including computer hardware.

The ability to use the funding for professional conferences and research equipment gives fellows additional flexibility in supporting their academic development.

3. Bloomberg Mentorship

Recipients will be connected with Bloomberg mentors.

This mentorship component provides fellows with professional connections to individuals working within Bloomberg’s research and technology environment while they continue their doctoral research.

4. Paid 14-Week Summer Internship

Fellows are required to complete a 14-week paid summer internship at Bloomberg for every year in which they are a fellow.

For the incoming fellowship cohort, the internship requirement begins in Summer 2027.

The internship will be research-focused and may take place in:

  • New York;
  • London; or
  • Toronto.

This component provides fellows with the opportunity to undertake practical research within Bloomberg while continuing to build their doctoral research experience.

5. Potential Fellowship Renewal for Up to Three Years

Recipients may have the opportunity to renew the Bloomberg fellowship annually for up to three years.

However, renewal is not automatic and remains at Bloomberg’s discretion.

Who Is Eligible for the Bloomberg Data Science Ph.D. Fellowship?

Bloomberg has established specific eligibility requirements that applicants should review carefully before preparing an application.

Full-Time Doctoral Student Requirement

Applicants must be full-time doctoral students during the 2027–2028 academic year.

They must also have an expected Ph.D. graduation date in or before the end of 2030.

Continued Full-Time Enrollment

Successful applicants must remain enrolled as full-time students throughout the duration of the grant.

Bloomberg states that if a fellow fails to maintain full-time student status, the remaining portion of the grant will be forfeited.

Academic Year Kickoff Event

Recipients are required to attend the fellowship’s academic-year kickoff event each fall at Bloomberg Headquarters in New York, unless Bloomberg conducts the event entirely online.

Bloomberg will cover expenses associated with the fellow’s attendance at this event.

Mandatory Summer Research Internship

Recipients must complete a 14-week summer internship during each year of their Bloomberg fellowship.

Internships may take place in:

  • New York;
  • London; or
  • Toronto.

Bloomberg states that these are paid, research-focused internships.

Restrictions on Other Industry Fellowships

Recipients cannot simultaneously receive support from another industry fellowship during the Bloomberg fellowship.

However, Bloomberg indicates that non-industry funding may be permitted on a case-by-case basis.

Outside Employment Restrictions

Fellows may not be employed outside their university during the fellowship unless they have received explicit permission from Bloomberg.

These requirements mean applicants should carefully review any existing funding arrangements, employment responsibilities or external fellowship commitments before applying.

Important U.S. Visa and Work Authorization Requirement

International applicants should pay particular attention to Bloomberg’s visa policy.

Bloomberg will not provide sponsorship for any U.S. visa for this fellowship.

Applicants who already possess self-sponsored work authorization covering the full internship or fellowship period may be eligible. Bloomberg provides examples including F-1 OPT or another Employment Authorization Document (EAD).

Because the fellowship requires an internship and may involve activities in the United States, prospective international applicants should carefully assess whether they can meet the applicable work authorization requirements before submitting an application.

Required Application Documents

Applications for the Bloomberg Data Science Ph.D. Fellowship must contain several documents.

Applicants need to prepare:

1. Curriculum Vitae

A current curriculum vitae (CV) must be submitted.

Applicants should ensure that their CV accurately presents their academic background, doctoral research, research experience, publications and other relevant academic or technical accomplishments.

2. Research Proposal

Applicants must submit a two-page research proposal, excluding references.

The proposal should describe the applicant’s proposed work and must be written for a technical audience.

Importantly, Bloomberg requires applicants to follow the formatting guidelines provided in its designated Overleaf application template.

Failure to comply with these formatting requirements will result in the application not being reviewed.

Applicants should therefore treat the formatting requirements as mandatory rather than optional.

3. Reference Letter

Applicants must obtain a reference letter from their:

  • Current advisor; or
  • Proposed advisor.

Applicants may also include an additional referee if desired.

During the application process, applicants will be asked to provide their referee’s contact information. The referee will subsequently receive an invitation allowing them to upload their recommendation letter through the application system.

All reference letters must be uploaded by the application deadline.

Bloomberg explicitly states that ensuring the reference letters are submitted on time is the applicant’s responsibility.

Incomplete Applications Will Not Be Considered

Applicants should carefully check their submissions before the deadline.

Bloomberg states that incomplete proposals will not be considered.

Candidates should therefore allow sufficient time before the deadline to:

  • Finalize their research proposal;
  • Check the required formatting;
  • Update their curriculum vitae;
  • Enter referee information;
  • Confirm that reference letters have been submitted; and
  • Complete the online application.

Waiting until the final hours could create unnecessary risks, particularly because reference letters must also be received before the deadline.

Bloomberg Data Science Ph.D. Fellowship Application Deadline

The application deadline for the Bloomberg Data Science Ph.D. Fellowship is:

Friday, September 25, 2026, at 11:59 PM Anywhere on Earth (AoE).

Applicants must upload their proposal and all necessary documents before this deadline.

Importantly, reference letters are subject to the same deadline and must also have been submitted before applications close.

When Will Successful Applicants Be Announced?

Bloomberg expects to inform fellowship recipients by:

Friday, December 18, 2026.

Applicants should therefore monitor the contact details used in their applications for communications relating to the outcome of the selection process.

How to Apply for the Bloomberg Data Science Ph.D. Fellowship

Applications are submitted online through Bloomberg’s designated fellowship application platform.

Applicants should:

  1. Review the fellowship eligibility criteria carefully.
  2. Confirm that they will be a full-time doctoral student during the 2027–2028 academic year.
  3. Confirm that their expected Ph.D. graduation date is no later than the end of 2030.
  4. Review Bloomberg’s listed research topics and assess the relevance of their proposed research.
  5. Prepare an updated curriculum vitae.
  6. Develop a two-page technical research proposal.
  7. Format the research proposal according to Bloomberg’s required Overleaf template.
  8. Identify an advisor or proposed advisor who can provide the required reference letter.
  9. Provide the referee’s contact details through the application system.
  10. Complete and submit the online application.
  11. Follow up with the referee to ensure the recommendation letter is uploaded before the deadline.
  12. Ensure the complete application is submitted no later than September 25, 2026, at 11:59 PM AoE.

Application portal: https://softconf.com/p/Bloomberg2027/

The source page contains an inconsistency worth noting: the detailed deadline section directs applicants to the Bloomberg2027 submission portal, while some “Apply Now” buttons shown elsewhere on the page link to a Bloomberg2026 portal. Because the 2027–2028 fellowship deadline section specifically directs candidates to Bloomberg2027, applicants should carefully verify the correct portal on Bloomberg’s official fellowship page before submitting.

Questions About the Application Process

Applicants with questions about the fellowship application process can contact the Bloomberg Data Science Ph.D. Fellowship grant program organizers at:

rdml@bloomberg.net

Bloomberg also notes that because of the volume of applications received, it cannot guarantee individual feedback on submitted proposals.

Why the Bloomberg Data Science Ph.D. Fellowship Is a Significant Opportunity

For doctoral researchers working in artificial intelligence, machine learning, data science and related disciplines, this fellowship offers more than conventional research funding.

The combination of full tuition funding, a USD 45,000 stipend, mentorship and a paid research internship creates a program that supports both academic progress and professional development.

The opportunity may be especially valuable to researchers interested in translating academic research into practical applications. Bloomberg’s areas of interest encompass several rapidly developing areas of AI and machine learning, ranging from agentic AI and large language models to multimodal systems, information retrieval, trustworthy AI and AI applications for finance.

The potential to renew the fellowship for up to three years also makes it particularly noteworthy for eligible doctoral researchers seeking longer-term research support, although continued funding remains at Bloomberg’s discretion.

Key Dates at a Glance

  • Academic year: 2027–2028
  • Application deadline: Friday, September 25, 2026
  • Deadline time: 11:59 PM Anywhere on Earth (AoE)
  • Reference letter deadline: September 25, 2026, before the application closes
  • Award notification: By Friday, December 18, 2026
  • First required summer internship: Summer 2027
  • Internship duration: 14 weeks
  • Potential fellowship duration: Renewable annually for up to three years at Bloomberg’s discretion.

APPLY NOW

Conclusion

The Bloomberg Data Science Ph.D. Fellowship 2027–2028 provides an outstanding funding and professional development opportunity for full-time doctoral students conducting research relevant to data science, artificial intelligence, machine learning and Bloomberg’s broader areas of technical interest.

Selected fellows will benefit from 100% tuition coverage, a USD 45,000 stipend, Bloomberg mentorship and a paid 14-week research internship, with the possibility of annual fellowship renewal for up to three years at Bloomberg’s discretion.

Applicants should pay particular attention to the program’s eligibility conditions, including continued full-time doctoral enrollment, restrictions on other industry fellowships and outside employment, the mandatory internship requirement and Bloomberg’s policy that it will not sponsor U.S. visas.

Candidates should also begin coordinating with their referees well before the deadline because recommendation letters must be received as part of the completed application.

The final deadline to submit a complete application is Friday, September 25, 2026, at 11:59 PM AoE. Eligible Ph.D. researchers interested in advancing research in AI, machine learning, data science and related fields should carefully review the requirements and prepare their applications ahead of the closing date.

Visit the OFY website for more Fellowship Opportunities.

item.content:encoded:
The Pandemic Fund Technical Advisory Panel (TAP) is inviting qualified experts to apply to serve as members of its Technical Advisory Panel. This opportunity is designed for professionals with strong technical expertise and relevant professional experience who can contribute to the work of the Pandemic Fund.

The application process is intended to help assess applicants based on their technical expertise, professional experience, geographic experience, and multisectoral experience. Selected experts will have the opportunity to contribute their knowledge and experience to the TAP’s work in supporting the Pandemic Fund.

Prospective applicants are encouraged to prepare their current CV and allow enough time to complete the application, particularly the short narrative questions included in the form.

Pandemic Fund Technical Advisory Panel Expert Opportunity 2026

The Technical Advisory Panel plays an important role in supporting the Pandemic Fund. The expert application is therefore intended for professionals who can demonstrate relevant knowledge, experience, and expertise that may contribute to the Panel’s work.

According to the application information, the assessment will consider several dimensions of an applicant’s background, including:

  • Technical expertise
  • Professional experience
  • Geographic experience
  • Multisectoral experience

Applicants should therefore carefully present their professional background and explain how their expertise and experience can contribute to the work of the Technical Advisory Panel.

What Is the Pandemic Fund TAP Expert Application?

The Technical Advisory Panel (TAP) Expert Application Form is an application process through which the Pandemic Fund can identify and assess individuals interested in serving as technical experts on the Panel.

The application is designed to gather information that can help the Pandemic Fund understand an applicant’s:

  1. Professional background
  2. Technical expertise
  3. Relevant professional experience
  4. Geographic experience
  5. Multisectoral experience
  6. Individual qualifications and experience

The information submitted through the application will be used by the Pandemic Fund to assess applicants for potential participation as experts on the TAP.

Who Should Consider Applying?

The opportunity is particularly relevant to professionals who have substantial or relevant expertise that could contribute to the work of a technical advisory panel supporting the Pandemic Fund.

Potential applicants should consider applying if their professional background demonstrates relevant technical knowledge, experience, geographic understanding, or multisectoral expertise.

Applicants should ensure that their application reflects their individual qualifications and experience, rather than relying on generic descriptions of their field or organisation.

Key Areas Considered in the Application

1. Technical Expertise

Applicants are expected to demonstrate the technical expertise they would bring to the Technical Advisory Panel.

When completing the application, candidates should clearly communicate the areas in which they have developed professional knowledge and expertise.

This may include explaining:

  • Their technical areas of specialization
  • Relevant professional experience
  • Areas in which they have provided technical input
  • How their expertise relates to the work of the Pandemic Fund

The application should provide an accurate representation of the applicant’s actual expertise.

2. Professional Experience

Professional experience is another important component of the assessment.

Applicants should be prepared to provide information that demonstrates their professional qualifications and experience. Their CV should complement the information provided in the application and give a clear picture of their professional background.

Candidates should ensure that their CV is current before submitting it.

3. Geographic Experience

The application also considers an applicant’s geographic experience.

This means candidates should clearly present relevant experience they have gained across geographic contexts, where applicable. Applicants with experience working across different geographic settings should ensure that this experience is appropriately reflected in their application.

4. Multisectoral Experience

The Pandemic Fund TAP application also seeks to assess multisectoral experience.

Applicants should therefore highlight relevant experience involving multiple sectors, disciplines, institutions, or professional areas where applicable.

This can help demonstrate an ability to understand complex issues from different perspectives and contribute to multidisciplinary discussions.

Application Materials Required

Applicants should prepare their materials before starting the application.

Current CV

Applicants are specifically advised to have their current CV ready for sharing.

The CV should accurately represent the applicant’s professional qualifications and experience.

Before submission, applicants should review their CV to ensure that:

  • It is up to date.
  • Relevant professional experience is clearly presented.
  • Technical expertise is appropriately reflected.
  • Geographic and multisectoral experience is included where relevant.
  • The information is consistent with the application form.

Narrative Responses

The application includes short narrative responses.

Applicants may wish to draft their responses separately before entering them into the online application form. This can be particularly useful for applicants who want to carefully structure their answers and ensure that they directly address the questions.

The application information estimates that completing the application will take approximately 20 minutes, although applicants should allow additional time to review their responses and prepare their CV.

How to Prepare a Strong Application

Applicants should avoid rushing the application simply because the form is estimated to take approximately 20 minutes.

A strong preparation process can include the following steps:

Step 1: Update Your CV

Prepare your most recent CV before opening the application form.

Make sure the CV accurately reflects your current professional experience, expertise, qualifications, and relevant areas of work.

Step 2: Review Your Professional Experience

Identify the experiences that are most relevant to the Technical Advisory Panel.

Pay particular attention to experience demonstrating:

  • Technical expertise
  • Professional leadership or responsibility
  • Geographic experience
  • Multisectoral collaboration
  • Relevant work connected to pandemic-related or broader health and development issues, where applicable

The source material does not provide a specific list of required technical disciplines, so applicants should focus on accurately presenting their own qualifications and experience rather than attempting to claim expertise that is not part of their background.

Step 3: Prepare the Narrative Responses

The application includes short narrative questions.

Applicants are encouraged to draft longer versions of their responses separately before entering them into the form. This allows candidates to refine their answers and ensure that the final responses are clear and directly relevant to the questions.

Step 4: Check Your Information

The Pandemic Fund specifically asks applicants to provide accurate and complete information throughout the application.

Before submitting, carefully check:

  • Names and contact information
  • Professional information
  • Qualifications
  • Experience
  • Narrative responses
  • CV
  • Any other required fields

Step 5: Submit Before the Deadline

Applicants should not wait until the final minutes to submit.

Late applications will not be considered, so candidates should allow sufficient time for completing the form, reviewing the information, and emailing the CV as required.

Application Deadline

The application will close on:

Friday, 18 September 2026 at 11:59 PM EST

This is a firm deadline according to the application information.

Applicants should make sure that both the completed application form and CV submission are completed according to the instructions before the deadline.

Important Instructions for Applicants

The application provides several important instructions that candidates should follow.

Submit the Completed Application and CV

Applicants are required to submit the completed application form and email their CV according to the directions in Section 10 before the deadline.

Submitting only one component may result in an incomplete application.

Provide Accurate Information

All information provided should be accurate and complete.

Applicants should ensure that their responses reflect their actual:

  • Qualifications
  • Professional experience
  • Technical expertise
  • Geographic experience
  • Multisectoral experience

Complete All Required Questions

Required questions must be completed before the application can be submitted.

Candidates should review the entire form carefully to make sure no required section has been overlooked.

Review Before Submission

Applicants are specifically encouraged to review their entries carefully before selecting “Submit.”

This final review is important because candidates should make sure their information is accurate, complete, and consistent with their CV.

Selection Process

The application information states that only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

This means submitting an application does not guarantee selection or appointment to the Technical Advisory Panel.

Applicants should therefore ensure that their submission clearly and accurately communicates the expertise and experience they could bring to the TAP.

Candidates should also understand that:

  • Only shortlisted applicants will be contacted.
  • Late applications will not be considered.
  • Incomplete applications will not be considered.
  • Applicants are responsible for ensuring that their information is accurate and complete.

Why This Opportunity Matters

Serving as an expert on the Pandemic Fund Technical Advisory Panel could provide an opportunity for qualified professionals to contribute their knowledge and experience to work supporting the Pandemic Fund.

For professionals with relevant expertise, the opportunity may allow them to bring their perspective to a technical advisory environment where technical, professional, geographic, and multisectoral experience are considered.

The opportunity may be particularly relevant for professionals interested in contributing their expertise to international work related to pandemic preparedness and the broader health and development landscape.

Click HERE to read more and apply.

Conclusion

The Pandemic Fund Technical Advisory Panel Expert Application 2026 provides an opportunity for qualified professionals to put forward their expertise for consideration to serve on the Pandemic Fund’s Technical Advisory Panel.

The application is designed to assess candidates across technical expertise, professional experience, geographic experience, and multisectoral experience. Applicants should therefore focus on presenting an accurate and compelling picture of the expertise and professional experience they can contribute.

Prospective applicants should prepare their current CV, carefully complete the required narrative responses, review all information before submission, and ensure that both the application and CV are submitted according to the stated instructions.

The application closes on Friday, 18 September 2026 at 11:59 PM EST, and the application information clearly states that late or incomplete applications will not be considered. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

item.content:encoded:
Applications are open for the Smithsonian James Smithson Fellowship Program 2027, a prestigious 12-month research opportunity for early-career postdoctoral researchers in the United States working across science, the humanities, and the arts.

Administered through the Smithsonian Institution’s Office of Academic Appointments and Internships, the James Smithson Fellowship Program provides researchers with an opportunity to pursue independent research while drawing on the Smithsonian’s extraordinary network of experts, research facilities, databases, and extensive collections.

For the 2027 cycle, the fellowship is centered on the theme “Regeneration.” Applicants are invited to develop interdisciplinary research proposals exploring how societies, environments, technologies, communities, and cultural traditions renew, recover, adapt, and maintain continuity over time.

Successful fellows will receive a $62,000 stipend and a research allowance of up to $5,000. Additional support may include a one-time travel allowance and a contribution toward health insurance costs.

The fellowship is primarily conducted in residence and lasts for 12 months. Appointments may begin as early as June 1, 2027, and must begin no later than May 1, 2028.

Importantly, this opportunity is restricted to eligible U.S. citizens, and applicants must generally be no more than five years beyond receiving their doctorate degree. Candidates holding terminal professional degrees may also be eligible.

James Smithson Fellowship Program 2027 Application Deadline

The application deadline for the 2027 James Smithson Fellowship Program is:

October 15, 2026, at 4:59 p.m. Eastern Time (ET).

Applicants must submit their complete applications through the Smithsonian Online Academic Appointment System (SOLAA) by the deadline.

Applicants should not wait until the final day to begin preparing their submission. The application requires a substantial research proposal, identification of a Smithsonian research advisor, references, transcripts, a budget, bibliography, curriculum vitae, and several other components.

In addition, applicants are responsible for ensuring that their required recommendation letters are submitted by the deadline.

About the James Smithson Fellowship Program

The James Smithson Fellowship Program was established to provide early-career postdoctoral researchers with an opportunity to deepen their disciplinary expertise while gaining a broader understanding of the relationship between academic scholarship, research, and public policy.

Rather than viewing research solely through the lens of an individual academic discipline, the program encourages fellows to examine the wider implications of their work.

The fellowship creates an immersive research environment where participants can work alongside Smithsonian researchers, interact with relevant collections and facilities, and consider how their research can contribute to wider conversations within society.

The program is particularly intended for a new generation of researchers and leaders interested in conducting innovative scholarship while exploring the potential policy implications and public significance of their research.

Fellows undertake independent empirical research within an interdisciplinary environment designed to encourage new ways of thinking, researching, and creating.

Theme for 2027: Regeneration

The theme of the 2027 James Smithson Fellowship is “Regeneration.”

The Smithsonian is inviting research proposals that examine how societies, environments, and cultural traditions renew and adapt over time.

Regeneration can occur in numerous forms and across many disciplines. The theme recognizes that renewal does not necessarily mean abandoning the past. Instead, regeneration can involve adapting to changing circumstances while preserving important elements of continuity.

Applicants are encouraged to explore processes including:

  • Restoration;
  • Resilience;
  • Adaptation;
  • Renewal;
  • Continuity;
  • Ecological recovery;
  • Cultural revitalization;
  • Community rebuilding;
  • Heritage conservation; and
  • Technological innovation.

The theme provides considerable room for interdisciplinary research.

What Does “Regeneration” Mean for the 2027 Fellowship?

The Smithsonian identifies several potential ways in which regeneration may be understood.

1. Restoration of Ecosystems

Researchers may investigate the ways natural environments recover, adapt, or are restored following environmental degradation, climate pressures, human activity, or other forms of disruption.

Research could potentially consider ecological adaptation, environmental resilience, restoration processes, conservation, or related questions.

2. Revitalization of Cultural Practices

Regeneration can also occur through the preservation, adaptation, and revitalization of cultural traditions.

Researchers working within history, anthropology, heritage, the humanities, arts, or related fields may consider how cultural knowledge and practices survive, change, or are renewed across generations and changing social environments.

3. Rebuilding Communities Following Disruption

The theme can extend to the ways communities rebuild and adapt following periods of disruption.

This creates opportunities to investigate resilience, social transformation, continuity, collective memory, recovery, and other processes through which communities respond to change.

4. Technological Innovation

Regeneration may also be considered through technological change and innovation.

Researchers may explore how technologies contribute to renewal, adaptation, preservation, resilience, or transformation across societies and environments.

These examples are not necessarily exhaustive. The broad nature of the theme allows researchers from science, the humanities, and the arts to approach regeneration through different disciplinary and interdisciplinary perspectives.

What Are the Goals of the James Smithson Fellowship?

The fellowship is designed to provide participants with several significant opportunities.

Fellows can:

  • Access Smithsonian facilities;
  • Work with extensive Smithsonian collections;
  • Utilize relevant Smithsonian databases;
  • Engage with Smithsonian research experts;
  • Encounter perspectives from multiple disciplines;
  • Conduct independent research;
  • Explore connections between academic scholarship and public policy;
  • Consider the wider implications of their research;
  • Develop skills that can help inform policy conversations; and
  • Deepen their disciplinary expertise within an innovative research environment.

The fellowship therefore goes beyond simply providing financial support for a research project.

It places researchers within the wider intellectual environment of the Smithsonian and encourages them to consider how their work connects with broader academic, cultural, scientific, societal, and policy questions.

Who Is Eligible for the James Smithson Fellowship Program 2027?

The James Smithson Fellowship Program is open to postdoctoral researchers in science, the humanities, and the arts.

Applicants must satisfy the program’s eligibility requirements.

Candidates must:

  • Be U.S. citizens;
  • Be postdoctoral researchers in science, the humanities, or the arts;
  • Generally be no more than five years beyond receipt of their doctorate degree; and
  • Meet the other requirements of the fellowship.

Candidates with terminal professional degrees are also eligible to apply.

Applicants should carefully review the official program guidelines before submitting an application to confirm their eligibility.

Smithsonian Research Advisor Requirement

One of the most important requirements of the James Smithson Fellowship is the identification of an appropriate Smithsonian research advisor.

Applicants are required to identify a Smithsonian expert listed in the Smithsonian Opportunities for Research and Study (SORS) guide who can serve as their research advisor during the fellowship.

This is not an optional component.

Only applicants who have identified a research advisor will be reviewed for the fellowship.

Applicants should therefore make identifying an appropriate advisor one of the first steps in preparing their application.

Before submitting an application, candidates should contact their prospective research advisor to:

  1. Introduce themselves and their proposed research;
  2. Determine whether the Smithsonian expert’s research interests and expertise are a good fit for the project;
  3. Confirm that the expert is available to serve as an advisor during the proposed fellowship period; and
  4. Discuss the research proposal and, where appropriate, anticipated research costs.

Applicants are strongly encouraged to correspond with their proposed Smithsonian advisor while developing their proposal.

Fellowship Duration and Starting Dates

The James Smithson Fellowship appointment lasts for:

12 months.

The fellowship is described as primarily in-residence, providing fellows with an immersive opportunity to engage with Smithsonian researchers, collections, facilities, and other relevant resources.

Appointments may commence:

  • As early as June 1, 2027;
  • No later than May 1, 2028.

Applicants should take these dates into account when preparing their proposed research timetable.

James Smithson Fellowship Stipend and Research Funding

Successful fellows receive significant financial support during the 12-month appointment.

Fellowship Stipend

Each fellow receives:

$62,000 stipend

Research Allowance

Fellows also receive:

Up to $5,000 in research allowance

The research allowance can support eligible costs associated with conducting the proposed research.

Applicants are required to prepare a budget and justification addressing expenses such as:

  • Equipment;
  • Supplies;
  • Research-related travel; and
  • Other support necessary to conduct the research.

The research budget should not include stipend or relocation costs.

Funding for direct hires may not be included.

Applicants are encouraged to discuss anticipated research costs with their proposed Smithsonian advisor before submitting their application.

If a research project requires more funding than the maximum $5,000 research allowance, the applicant must explain where the additional funding will come from.

Potential Additional Support

Additional fellowship support may include:

  • A one-time travel allowance; and
  • A contribution toward health insurance costs.

Applicants should consult the official program information for applicable conditions surrounding additional support.

How to Apply for the James Smithson Fellowship Program 2027

Applications must be submitted electronically through the Smithsonian Online Academic Appointment System (SOLAA).

The complete application must be submitted by October 15, 2026, at 4:59 p.m. ET.

Applicants should allow sufficient time to prepare all required documents and coordinate with their Smithsonian research advisor and references.

Required Application Documents

The James Smithson Fellowship application requires several detailed components.

1. Research Abstract

Applicants must provide an abstract summarizing their proposed research.

The abstract must be:

  • No more than one page; and
  • Double-spaced.

The abstract should clearly communicate the core research question, approach, and significance of the proposed project.

2. Research Proposal

Applicants must prepare a detailed research proposal.

The proposal must be:

  • No more than six pages;
  • Double-spaced;
  • Prepared on approximately 8.5 x 11-inch (210 mm x 297 mm) paper;
  • Formatted with one-inch margins; and
  • Written using a font no smaller than 11 point.

The six-page limit excludes other application components such as the abstract and bibliography, but includes images, tables, and similar materials contained within the proposal.

The proposal must address several important areas.

Proposed Research and Methodology

Applicants should describe the research they intend to conduct at the Smithsonian and explain the methodology they will use.

Potential Public Policy Implications

A significant component of the fellowship is the relationship between scholarship and public policy.

Applicants must therefore explain how their proposed research could potentially inform public policy.

Importance of the Research

Applicants should discuss why their research matters.

This should address its importance both:

  • Within the broader academic or professional discipline; and
  • In relation to the applicant’s own scholarly goals.

Why the Smithsonian Is Necessary

The proposal must justify why the research should be conducted at the Smithsonian Institution.

Applicants should explain how they plan to use relevant Smithsonian:

  • Collections;
  • Facilities;
  • Databases;
  • Research expertise;
  • Staff; and/or
  • Other resources.

A strong proposal should demonstrate a meaningful connection between the project and the resources available through the Smithsonian.

Smithsonian Principal Research Advisor

Applicants must identify the Smithsonian research staff member who will serve as their principal advisor.

Again, identification of an eligible Smithsonian advisor is mandatory.

Applicants are strongly encouraged to communicate with their proposed advisor while developing the research proposal.

3. Research Timetable

Applicants must submit an estimated timetable covering the entire fellowship period.

The timetable should explain when the major phases of the proposed research are expected to occur.

A clear timetable can help demonstrate that the research project is realistic and can be completed within the fellowship period.

4. Budget and Budget Justification

Applicants must submit a budget explaining anticipated research expenses.

Eligible categories can include:

  • Equipment;
  • Supplies;
  • Research-related travel expenses; and
  • Other support required to conduct the research.

Applicants cannot use this budget to include direct hires.

The budget also excludes the fellowship stipend and relocation costs.

If anticipated research expenses exceed the maximum $5,000 research allowance, applicants must identify and explain the source of additional funding.

5. Bibliography

Applicants must provide a bibliography covering literature relevant to their proposed research.

The bibliography must not exceed:

Two pages.

It should demonstrate familiarity with relevant scholarship and provide intellectual context for the proposed research.

6. Curriculum Vitae

Applicants must provide a current curriculum vitae.

The CV should highlight areas including:

  • Education;
  • Expertise;
  • Academic and professional achievements;
  • Honors;
  • Publications; and
  • Research interests.

The CV should not exceed five pages.

Applicants whose native language is not English must also describe their proficiency in:

  • Reading English;
  • Speaking English; and
  • Writing English.

7. Academic Transcripts

Applicants must submit transcripts from their terminal degree institution or institutions.

Unofficial transcripts are acceptable.

Applicants should ensure that the submitted documentation appropriately reflects their academic background and qualifications.

8. Two References and Letters of Recommendation

Applicants must provide the:

  • Name; and
  • Email address

of two non-Smithsonian individuals who are familiar with their research.

These references will be asked to submit confidential letters of recommendation online.

Applicants may provide their references with:

  • A copy of their research proposal; and
  • The Smithsonian’s Letter to Reference document.

Applicants are responsible for ensuring that both recommendation letters are submitted by the application deadline.

This is particularly important because applications containing fewer than two letters of recommendation may not be considered.

Candidates should therefore contact their references well before October 15 rather than waiting until the application deadline approaches.

How Applications Will Be Evaluated

Applications will be reviewed by Smithsonian scholars working in appropriate fields.

The selection process considers several factors.

Innovation and Relationship to the 2027 Theme

Reviewers will examine the extent to which the proposed research is innovative and meaningfully connected to the theme of Regeneration.

Applicants should therefore make the relationship between their research and the fellowship theme clear within their proposal.

Potential Public Policy Relevance

Reviewers will consider how effectively the proposal addresses the potential for the research to inform public policy.

Applicants should demonstrate that they have considered the wider implications of their work rather than simply describing an academic research project.

Ability to Conduct the Research

The selection process will consider whether the applicant has the knowledge, skills, experience, and academic background necessary to successfully conduct the proposed project.

Feasibility

Reviewers will assess whether the research can realistically be completed within the requested fellowship period.

This makes the research timetable, methodology, scope, and project design particularly important.

Relevance of Smithsonian Resources

Applicants will be evaluated on the extent to which Smithsonian research staff and institutional resources can contribute to the proposed research.

Candidates should clearly demonstrate why conducting the project through the Smithsonian would provide meaningful value.

Alignment With Career Goals

Reviewers will consider how the fellowship aligns with the applicant’s broader career objectives.

Applicants should therefore think carefully about how the experience will contribute to their development as researchers and future leaders.

Leadership Potential

A candidate’s potential for leadership will also be assessed, including evidence demonstrated through previous performance and accomplishments.

Academic Record

The quality of the applicant’s academic record forms another part of the selection process.

Taken together, these criteria mean that a competitive application should combine a strong academic profile with an innovative, feasible research project that clearly connects with the theme of Regeneration, makes meaningful use of Smithsonian resources, and demonstrates potential relevance to public policy.

Important Restrictions for Smithsonian Employees and Contractors

Current employees and contractors of the Smithsonian Institution cannot hold a Smithsonian fellowship while simultaneously employed or contracted by the institution.

The Smithsonian also states that former employees or contractors generally need one year of separation before applying for a fellowship, unless prior approval is obtained from the Office of Academic Appointments and Internships.

Anyone affected by these conditions should consult the official fellowship guidelines or contact the Office of Academic Appointments and Internships for clarification.

Equal Employment Opportunity and Non-Discrimination

The Smithsonian Institution states that it does not discriminate based on:

  • Race;
  • Color;
  • Religion;
  • Sex, including gender identity, sexual orientation, and pregnancy;
  • National origin;
  • Age for individuals aged 40 or older;
  • Disability;
  • Genetic information;
  • Parental status; or
  • Military service.

Applicants should note, however, that the James Smithson Fellowship itself has a citizenship eligibility requirement: candidates must be U.S. citizens.

Important Dates at a Glance

Prospective applicants should keep the following dates in mind:

  • Application deadline: October 15, 2026
  • Application closing time: 4:59 p.m. ET
  • Earliest fellowship start date: June 1, 2027
  • Latest fellowship start date: May 1, 2028
  • Fellowship duration: 12 months

Applicants outside the Eastern Time Zone should pay particular attention to the 4:59 p.m. ET closing time and submit well in advance to avoid time-zone confusion or last-minute technical difficulties.

Key Fellowship Details at a Glance

Program: James Smithson Fellowship Program 2027

Host Institution: Smithsonian Institution

2027 Theme: Regeneration

Research Fields: Science, humanities, and arts

Fellowship Duration: 12 months, primarily in residence

Stipend: $62,000

Research Allowance: Up to $5,000

Additional Potential Support: One-time travel allowance and contribution toward health insurance costs

Eligibility: Eligible U.S. citizen postdoctoral researchers and candidates with qualifying terminal professional degrees

Application Platform: Smithsonian Online Academic Appointment System (SOLAA)

Deadline: October 15, 2026, at 4:59 p.m. ET

Earliest Start: June 1, 2027

Latest Start: May 1, 2028

Important Tips Before Applying

Because this is a research-intensive fellowship, applicants should begin preparation well ahead of the deadline.

In particular, candidates should:

  1. Confirm their eligibility before preparing the full application. The program is restricted to eligible U.S. citizens and primarily targets postdoctoral researchers within five years of receiving their doctorate.
  2. Identify a Smithsonian research advisor early. This is mandatory, and applications without an identified advisor will not be reviewed.
  3. Contact the prospective advisor before applying. Confirm that the Smithsonian expert is an appropriate fit and is available during the proposed fellowship period.
  4. Build a clear connection to the theme of Regeneration. Reviewers specifically evaluate how innovative the proposed research is and how it relates to the annual theme.
  5. Explain the public policy dimension. Applicants should clearly articulate how their research could potentially inform public policy.
  6. Demonstrate why the Smithsonian is essential to the project. The proposal should identify specific experts, facilities, collections, databases, or other resources relevant to the research.
  7. Prepare a realistic 12-month timetable. The selection process considers whether the project can reasonably be completed during the requested period.
  8. Coordinate with references early. Two confidential recommendation letters are required, and the applicant is responsible for ensuring they arrive on time.
  9. Review the research budget carefully. If anticipated research expenses exceed the $5,000 allowance, explain how the additional costs will be funded.
  10. Submit before the final deadline. Applications must be completed through SOLAA by October 15, 2026, at 4:59 p.m. ET.

How to Apply

Eligible applicants should complete their applications through the Smithsonian Online Academic Appointment System (SOLAA):

https://solaa.si.edu/

Before beginning the application, candidates should also carefully review the official James Smithson Fellowship Program Guidelines:

https://fellowships.si.edu/james-smithson-fellowship

Applicants looking for a potential Smithsonian research advisor should consult the Smithsonian Opportunities for Research and Study (SORS) resources:

https://fellowships.si.edu/SORS

Questions about the fellowship may be directed to the Smithsonian Institution’s Office of Academic Appointments and Internships at:

InternsAndFellows@si.edu

APPLY NOW

Conclusion

The Smithsonian James Smithson Fellowship Program 2027 offers an exceptional opportunity for eligible early-career U.S. researchers to pursue ambitious independent research within one of the world’s most prominent research, museum, scientific, historical, and cultural institutions.

With a $62,000 stipend, up to $5,000 in research funding, potential additional travel and health insurance support, and access to Smithsonian researchers, facilities, databases, and extensive collections, the fellowship provides much more than financial support. It gives researchers an environment in which they can deepen their expertise, work across disciplinary boundaries, and examine the wider societal and public policy significance of their scholarship.

The 2027 theme, Regeneration, creates a particularly broad interdisciplinary framework. Researchers may investigate ecological restoration, cultural revitalization, community resilience, adaptation, technological innovation, heritage conservation, continuity, or other processes through which societies, environments, and traditions renew and transform over time.

A particularly important step for prospective applicants is finding an appropriate Smithsonian research advisor. Since applications without an identified advisor will not be reviewed, candidates should begin exploring Smithsonian experts and establishing contact well before preparing their final submission.

Eligible researchers interested in the program should begin preparing their proposal, identifying an advisor, contacting references, developing their research budget and timetable, and gathering the necessary academic documents as early as possible.

All applications must be submitted through SOLAA by October 15, 2026, at 4:59 p.m. ET.

Visit the OFY website for more Fellowship Opportunities.

item.content:encoded:
The NASA Fellowship Activity provides opportunities designed to strengthen the next generation of scientists, engineers, researchers and other STEM professionals while supporting research and education that contribute to the missions of the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA).

Through its fellowship activities, NASA supports research, graduate-level education, hands-on experience and workforce development in science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM). The initiative forms part of NASA’s wider commitment to developing a highly skilled workforce capable of contributing to research, innovation, aeronautics, science and the continued advancement of space exploration.

Each year, NASA Fellowships awards research grants, as authorized by Congress, to Minority Serving Institutions (MSIs) through funding from the Minority University Research and Education Project (MUREP). The fellowship activity is intended to help prepare graduate-level students for research careers by combining academic development with practical experience and workforce training.

NASA also partners with The National GEM Consortium, providing another important pathway for undergraduate and graduate students pursuing disciplines relevant to NASA’s missions.

For students interested in engineering, computer science, physical sciences, mathematics, data science, environmental science and numerous other STEM disciplines, NASA’s fellowship ecosystem provides a valuable starting point for identifying graduate education, research and professional development opportunities.

About the NASA Fellowship Activity

NASA Fellowships are designed to help develop a well-trained STEM workforce capable of contributing to the United States’ scientific, technological and space exploration priorities.

The fellowship activity has a strong emphasis on preparing graduate-level students for careers in research. Participants and institutions can benefit from opportunities that connect academic learning with practical research experience, workforce preparation and exposure to areas relevant to NASA’s work.

NASA’s fellowship activities also support the broader development of:

  • Faculty members;
  • Undergraduate students;
  • Graduate students;
  • Researchers;
  • STEM professionals; and
  • Academic institutions involved in research and education.

Through NASA’s partnership with The National GEM Consortium, students in disciplines needed to advance NASA’s missions can gain access to graduate education, industry experience and professional development opportunities.

The overall goal extends beyond providing financial assistance. NASA Fellowships contribute to the development of a pipeline of talented scientists, engineers and researchers who can potentially advance innovation and discovery in areas connected with NASA’s work.

NASA Fellowships and the Minority University Research and Education Project

An important component of NASA’s Fellowship Activity is its relationship with the Minority University Research and Education Project (MUREP).

Each year, NASA awards research grants to Minority Serving Institutions using MUREP funds. These investments are authorized by Congress and are intended to strengthen research capacity, STEM education and workforce development.

MUREP supports NASA’s efforts to engage academic institutions and students while building pathways into STEM research and related careers.

Prospective applicants should understand that these institutional research grants are distinct from individual graduate fellowship opportunities. Students looking for an individual fellowship should carefully review the specific program through which they intend to apply.

NASA and The National GEM Consortium Partnership

One of the major pathways highlighted through NASA Fellowships is its partnership with The National GEM Consortium.

GEM provides opportunities for students pursuing master’s and Ph.D.-level education in engineering and science. The program connects graduate education with employers, universities and practical professional experience.

The GEM Fellowship Program is designed to promote opportunities for individuals to enter industry at the graduate level, particularly in areas including:

  • Research and development;
  • Product development;
  • Engineering;
  • Scientific research;
  • Advanced technical careers; and
  • Academia.

GEM provides MS and Ph.D. students with access to participating engineering and science employers and universities.

This structure can be particularly valuable for students seeking a graduate education experience that combines academic study with professional exposure.

GEM Fellowship Programs

The National GEM Consortium identifies fellowship opportunities at both the Master’s and Ph.D. levels in engineering and science.

Through the program, eligible fellows may receive financial support for graduate education while gaining practical work experience with participating employers.

The structure helps connect three important components of STEM career development:

  1. Graduate-level academic education;
  2. Financial support for advanced study; and
  3. Practical industry experience.

This combination allows fellows to develop academic expertise while simultaneously gaining experience that may prepare them for research, engineering, technology and other highly technical careers.

GEM Fellowship Benefits

The exact financial package and benefits depend on the fellowship classification and sponsorship arrangement.

Employer Fellows

For Employer Fellows, university sponsorship is required, and applicants must be available for selection by a participating employer.

According to the GEM Fellowship Program information, benefits can include:

  • A minimum total stipend of $16,000 over the entire Master’s program;
  • Up to two paid summer internships with a GEM Employer Member; and
  • Full tuition and fees provided by a GEM University Member.

The combination of tuition assistance, stipend support and paid internships makes the fellowship particularly valuable for students seeking both academic and professional development.

University Fellows

University Fellows may receive:

  • Full tuition and fees provided by a participating GEM Member University.

Associate Fellows

Associate Fellows may receive:

  • Full tuition and fees from the GEM Member University;
  • At least $8,000 per year in stipend support for Master’s students; and
  • At least $16,000 per year in stipend support for Ph.D. students.

Applicants should note that University and Associate Fellows are nominated by participating universities rather than selected as an applicant-chosen fellowship classification.

Practical Summer Internship Experience

Practical professional experience is an important component of the GEM Fellowship.

For applicable GEM Fellows, the summer internship with a GEM Employer represents the initial phase of the fellowship program. Acceptance of the relevant employment validates the fellowship.

Confirmed GEM Fellowship internships generally must be completed over a 10- to 12-week period during the summer, normally between May and August, or potentially into September for universities operating on a quarter system.

This work experience gives fellows an opportunity to apply their academic knowledge in professional environments while building experience relevant to advanced STEM careers.

General GEM Fellowship Eligibility Requirements

Students interested in the GEM pathway highlighted by NASA should carefully review its eligibility requirements.

For the program described by GEM, applicants must:

  • Be a senior or graduate of an accredited engineering or computer science program at the time of application;
  • Have a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.8 on a 4.0 scale; and
  • Contractually agree to intern for two summers with the sponsoring GEM Employer, beginning in the summer following sponsorship.

Additional requirements apply elsewhere in the program rules and should be reviewed before an application is submitted.

Citizenship Requirement

The GEM Fellowship has an important citizenship requirement.

Applicants must be either:

  • A United States citizen; or
  • A United States permanent resident

at the time they submit their application.

International students who do not hold U.S. citizenship or U.S. permanent resident status therefore do not meet this stated GEM citizenship requirement.

Applicants should not automatically assume that this citizenship rule applies to every NASA graduate or postdoctoral opportunity. Other NASA opportunities may establish their own eligibility requirements, and candidates should review the specific solicitation or program before applying.

Is the GRE Required?

The Graduate Record Examination, commonly known as the GRE, is not required for the GEM Fellowship application.

However, GEM strongly encourages students considering STEM graduate programs to take the GRE because individual universities or graduate programs may have their own admissions requirements.

Applicants who already have GRE results may submit their scores. Candidates should therefore separately review the admission requirements of every graduate program to which they intend to apply.

University Application Requirement

Applying for the fellowship does not replace applying to graduate school.

Applicants are required to apply directly to a minimum of three GEM Member Universities’ STEM graduate departments.

The deadline identified for applying to the three GEM Member Universities is January 15 or the relevant STEM graduate department’s deadline, whichever comes earlier.

Applicants must ultimately be admitted to a GEM Member University’s graduate program with confirmed departmental funding support before the GEM Fellowship can be awarded.

This requirement is particularly important because submitting only the GEM Fellowship application is not sufficient.

Even undergraduate students whose current university has indicated that it may support them as a GEM Fellow are generally still required to apply to three GEM Member Universities. A limited exception exists for certain applicants already matriculating in the same graduate program for which they are seeking financial support.

Eligible STEM Disciplines

The GEM Fellowship covers an extensive range of science, technology, engineering and mathematics disciplines.

Examples identified by GEM include, but are not limited to:

  • Aeronautical Engineering;
  • Aerospace Engineering;
  • Agricultural Engineering;
  • Analytical Chemistry;
  • Anatomy;
  • Automotive Engineering;
  • Biochemistry;
  • Bioengineering;
  • Biology;
  • Biomedical Engineering;
  • Chemical Engineering;
  • Chemistry;
  • Civil Engineering;
  • Computer Engineering;
  • Computer Science;
  • Data Science;
  • Electrical Engineering;
  • Environmental Engineering;
  • Environmental Science;
  • Industrial Engineering;
  • Information Systems;
  • Inorganic Chemistry;
  • Manufacturing Engineering;
  • Materials Engineering;
  • Materials Science;
  • Mathematics;
  • Mechanical Engineering;
  • Metallurgical Engineering;
  • Nuclear Engineering;
  • Operations Research;
  • Organic Chemistry;
  • Petroleum Engineering;
  • Physics;
  • Robotics and Engineering;
  • Structural Engineering; and
  • Systems Engineering.

Because this list is not exhaustive, students in related STEM fields should review the current eligible disciplines and program rules before determining whether their program qualifies.

How to Apply for NASA Fellowship Opportunities

NASA directs prospective applicants to different resources depending on the type of opportunity they are seeking.

1. GEM Fellowship Opportunities

Students interested in GEM Fellowship opportunities should visit The National GEM Consortium’s GEM Fellowship Program.

The current program information indicates that the GEM application is open and provides access to the eGEM application system.

Applicants should carefully review:

  • Fellowship options;
  • Application instructions;
  • Rules and requirements;
  • Eligible disciplines;
  • Available resources;
  • Internship requirements; and
  • Frequently asked questions.

2. Planned NASA Solicitations

Applicants and institutions interested in planned NASA funding opportunities should consult NASA’s EONS Grant Forecasting webpage.

This resource provides information concerning planned solicitations and can help prospective applicants anticipate upcoming opportunities.

3. Graduate and Postdoctoral Opportunities

NASA directs individuals looking for other graduate and postdoctoral opportunities to its Learner Opportunities resources.

Because requirements can vary significantly between programs, prospective applicants should review each individual opportunity rather than assuming that GEM’s requirements apply to all NASA-supported fellowships.

Important Application Deadlines

The NASA Fellowship Activity information provided does not state one universal application deadline for all NASA Fellowships.

Similarly, the supplied GEM Fellowship Program information indicates that the GEM application is currently open but does not provide a single closing date for the fellowship application itself. Applicants should therefore check the current eGEM application portal and official program instructions for the applicable application-cycle deadline.

One important deadline is explicitly identified for the university application component:

GEM Member University application deadline: January 15 or the relevant STEM graduate department deadline, whichever is earlier.

Applicants should not wait until January 15 without checking their chosen departments because a department may impose an earlier deadline.

Important Considerations Before Applying

Prospective applicants should carefully understand the commitments associated with accepting a GEM Fellowship.

Employer Selection

Applicants may be contacted by multiple GEM employers during the selection process. However, the employer ultimately selects the applicant for sponsorship rather than the applicant selecting the sponsoring employer.

Once an applicant has been selected for sponsorship by a GEM Employer, another GEM Employer cannot subsequently select that applicant. If the applicant rejects the internship and sponsorship offer, this can amount to declining the GEM Fellowship.

Graduate School Commitment

Applicants should be prepared to begin or continue their graduate education as required.

GEM indicates that an applicant cannot knowingly accept the fellowship with the intention of deferring the beginning of graduate school to a later date. Candidates uncertain about their graduate education plans should communicate with the relevant employer and university representatives before making a commitment.

Fellowship and Other Funding

Receiving another funding opportunity does not necessarily mean a student cannot participate in GEM. However, GEM states that fellows cannot accept a competing fellowship alongside the GEM Fellowship, although certain supplemental fellowships may be permitted.

Applicants receiving multiple funding offers should confirm compatibility before accepting them.

Why Consider NASA-Connected STEM Fellowship Opportunities?

For aspiring scientists, engineers and researchers, NASA-associated fellowship pathways can provide more than financial assistance.

Depending on the specific program, potential advantages can include:

  • Support for graduate education;
  • Research experience;
  • Exposure to NASA-relevant STEM disciplines;
  • Workforce training;
  • Professional development;
  • Industry experience;
  • Paid internship opportunities;
  • Connections with participating employers;
  • Access to universities and research environments;
  • Opportunities to develop advanced technical skills; and
  • Preparation for careers in research, engineering, science, technology and academia.

NASA’s broader objective of preparing graduate students for research careers means these opportunities can serve as an important bridge between university education and advanced STEM careers.

About NASA

The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) is the United States government agency responsible for the nation’s civilian space program as well as major work in aeronautics and space research.

NASA describes its mission as exploring the unknown in air and space, innovating for the benefit of humanity and inspiring the world through discovery.

Its work spans areas including space exploration, Earth science, planetary science, astrophysics, aeronautics, technology development and human spaceflight.

Developing future generations of STEM professionals is therefore an important component of NASA’s long-term mission.

Where to Find More Information

Prospective applicants should use the official NASA and GEM resources for current requirements and application information.

For NASA Fellowship information, visit:

https://www.nasa.gov/learning-resources/internship-programs/nasa-fellowships/

For GEM Fellowship opportunities and application information, visit:

https://www.gemfellowship.org/gem-fellowship-program/

The GEM application portal is available through the eGEM system.

For planned NASA solicitations, applicants should consult NASA’s EONS Grant Forecasting webpage.

For other NASA graduate and postdoctoral opportunities, candidates should explore NASA’s Learner Opportunities resources.

Questions specifically concerning NASA Fellowships may also be directed to:

Fellowships@mail.nasa.gov

Conclusion

The NASA Fellowship Activity represents an important component of NASA’s investment in STEM education, research and workforce development. Through research grants to Minority Serving Institutions, graduate-level development activities and partnerships such as the collaboration with The National GEM Consortium, NASA helps create pathways for students, researchers and academic institutions to contribute to the future of science, technology, engineering and space exploration.

For eligible graduate students, the GEM Fellowship pathway can be particularly valuable because it combines academic financial assistance with practical industry experience. Depending on fellowship classification and sponsorship, support can include full tuition and fees, stipends and paid summer internships with participating GEM employers.

Prospective applicants should nevertheless distinguish between the broader NASA Fellowship Activity and specific programs such as GEM. Eligibility, citizenship, funding, academic requirements and deadlines can vary depending on the particular fellowship or solicitation.

Students interested in the GEM pathway should pay particular attention to the U.S. citizenship or permanent residency requirement, academic eligibility, internship commitments and the requirement to apply to at least three GEM Member University STEM graduate departments.

Most importantly, applicants should consult the official NASA and GEM websites before submitting an application to confirm the current application cycle, deadlines and program requirements.

For students who meet the applicable requirements and are serious about building advanced careers in engineering, science, research and technology, NASA-connected fellowship opportunities offer a pathway to combine graduate education, professional experience and participation in the broader STEM workforce supporting future innovation and exploration.

Visit the OFY website for more Fellowship Opportunities.
