item.content:encoded:
Applications are now open for the Co-operatives UK Youth Advisory Group 2026, a paid youth participation opportunity for young people aged 16 to 30 who want to help influence the future of the co-operative movement, strengthen youth participation, and contribute ideas on how co-operative values can respond to some of the challenges facing younger generations.

Established in 2024, the Youth Advisory Group, commonly referred to as the YAG, brings together young people from different backgrounds to provide strategic input into the work of Co-operatives UK and to develop independent projects designed to increase engagement among young people both within the co-operative movement and across wider society.

Importantly, applicants do not need to have previous experience with co-operatives. Applications are welcomed from young people already involved in co-operative organizations as well as those who are completely new to the movement.

Members of the Youth Advisory Group are paid for their time, reflecting both the commitment expected from participants and Co-operatives UK’s intention to reduce barriers that could otherwise prevent young people from participating.

Applications may be submitted in several formats. Candidates can respond through:

  • Written text
  • Video
  • Audio

The application process is designed to be accessible to people with different levels of experience and different communication styles.

Applications close at:

23:59 on Sunday, 6 September 2026.

Applicants must complete the official application form and send it to:

youth@uk.coop

About Co-operatives UK

Co-operatives UK is an organization representing and supporting the co-operative movement.

Co-operatives are organizations or businesses owned and controlled by their members rather than primarily by outside investors. Depending on the type of co-operative, members may include:

  • Workers
  • Consumers
  • Residents
  • Community members
  • Producers
  • Businesses
  • Other stakeholders

The broader co-operative movement is based on ideas such as:

  • Democratic participation
  • Shared ownership
  • Fairness
  • Community
  • Mutual support
  • Collective decision-making
  • Economic participation
  • Social responsibility

Co-operatives UK’s Youth Advisory Group is intended to ensure that younger people have a meaningful role in conversations about how these ideas should develop in the future.

What Is the Co-operatives UK Youth Advisory Group?

The Youth Advisory Group is a group of young people aged 16–30 who work with Co-operatives UK to bring youth perspectives into the organization’s work.

The group was established in:

2024

It was launched through Co-operatives UK’s National Youth Summit as part of the organization’s strategic commitment to:

Empowering young people.

The group has two broad functions:

  1. Providing strategic advice and youth perspectives to Co-operatives UK.
  2. Developing or supporting projects that increase young people’s participation in the co-operative movement.

The YAG is therefore more than a discussion forum.

Members are expected to contribute ideas, challenge assumptions, advocate for youth participation, and help connect co-operative principles with the priorities and experiences of younger generations.

Why the Youth Advisory Group Was Created

Co-operatives UK recognizes that young people face significant uncertainty in areas such as:

  • Employment
  • Economic security
  • Climate change
  • Community resilience
  • Housing
  • Business models
  • Social inequality
  • Participation in decision-making

At the same time, many young people may know relatively little about co-operatives and the alternative approaches they can provide to ownership, work, business, and community action.

The Youth Advisory Group was therefore created to help bridge this gap.

Its members can help Co-operatives UK understand:

  • What young people care about
  • What prevents young people from engaging with co-operatives
  • How co-operative ideas can be communicated more effectively
  • What types of opportunities would interest younger generations
  • How the movement can become more accessible and relevant

The Role of Youth Advisory Group Members

The official description of the Youth Advisory Group organizes its work around two major areas:

  1. Advise and enrich
  2. Advocate and engage

1. Advise and Enrich

Young people can bring perspectives that established organizations may not otherwise hear.

Youth Advisory Group members are therefore expected to help Co-operatives UK:

  • Understand younger generations
  • Generate new ideas
  • Challenge established ways of thinking
  • Improve youth participation
  • Make decisions that better reflect young people’s needs
  • Include youth perspectives in organizational discussions

The group provides strategic input into Co-operatives UK’s work.

This means members may be asked to comment on ideas, priorities, activities, communication, or wider questions affecting the co-operative movement.

Bringing New Perspectives

A central purpose of the YAG is to ensure that young people are not merely discussed as an audience but are included in conversations about the future of the movement.

Young members may bring perspectives shaped by:

  • Education
  • Employment
  • Entrepreneurship
  • Climate concerns
  • Community involvement
  • Social movements
  • Digital culture
  • Youth networks
  • Cost-of-living pressures
  • Changing expectations about work and business

These experiences can help established organizations identify blind spots and reconsider traditional approaches.

Championing Youth Voice

Youth Advisory Group members work alongside Co-operatives UK to:

Champion the youth voice.

This means advocating for young people to be meaningfully involved in the co-operative movement rather than included only symbolically.

Participants can help promote:

  • Youth participation
  • Youth leadership
  • Intergenerational collaboration
  • Representation
  • Accessible opportunities
  • New ways of engaging younger audiences

The group therefore serves as both an advisory mechanism and a platform for youth representation.

2. Advocate and Engage

The second major role of the Youth Advisory Group is advocacy.

Co-operatives UK notes that younger generations are facing an uncertain future, including challenges related to:

  • Climate anxiety
  • Job insecurity
  • Economic pressures

The organization believes that co-operative approaches can contribute to a fairer future but recognizes that many young people are not yet familiar with the co-operative movement.

Members of the YAG therefore help:

  • Raise awareness of co-operatives
  • Promote co-operative values
  • Connect with youth networks
  • Encourage participation
  • Explain alternative approaches to business and ownership
  • Increase engagement beyond existing co-operative communities

What Issues Might Interest Applicants?

Although applicants do not need to have a specific professional or academic background, the opportunity may be particularly attractive to young people interested in issues such as:

  • Fairness
  • Climate action
  • Community development
  • Social justice
  • Ethical business
  • Alternative business models
  • Youth empowerment
  • Sustainability
  • Social enterprise
  • Economic democracy
  • Employment
  • Community ownership

Candidates do not need to be experts in these issues.

The application is designed to identify young people who have ideas, motivation, relevant perspectives, or useful experiences to contribute.

You Do Not Need Previous Co-operative Experience

One of the most important features of the application call is that previous involvement with co-operatives is not required.

Applications are welcomed from:

  • Young people already active in co-operatives
  • Young people familiar with the movement
  • Young people with limited co-operative experience
  • Young people completely new to co-operatives

This makes the opportunity accessible to a broader range of applicants.

The group is intentionally designed to bring together people from across the co-operative landscape as well as people who may offer entirely new perspectives.

Members Are Paid for Their Time

Youth Advisory Group members are:

Paid for their time.

This is an important feature of the opportunity.

Co-operatives UK states that payment is intended to:

  • Recognize the commitment involved
  • Reduce barriers to participation
  • Value young people’s contributions
  • Support meaningful participation

The supplied call does not specify the exact payment rate or total amount.

Applicants should therefore consult the official information pack for precise details about:

  • Payment arrangements
  • Expected hours
  • Meeting frequency
  • Duration of membership
  • Other participation conditions

The National Youth Summit

The Youth Advisory Group was launched at the:

Co-operatives UK National Youth Summit

in 2024.

The National Youth Summit is an annual event intended to:

  • Increase young people’s understanding of co-operatives
  • Build enthusiasm for co-operative approaches
  • Create opportunities for learning
  • Provide networking opportunities
  • Bring young co-operators together

The establishment of the YAG created a more ongoing mechanism for young people to influence the organization beyond the annual summit.

Who Can Apply?

The main age requirement is clear:

Applicants must be aged 16 to 30.

The official announcement emphasizes that applications are welcomed from young people with:

All levels of experience and skills.

There is no requirement in the supplied call for applicants to hold:

  • A university degree
  • A professional qualification
  • Previous employment experience
  • Leadership experience
  • Previous co-operative membership

This makes the opportunity considerably more accessible than many formal youth leadership programmes.

Experience Level

Applicants may be:

  • Students
  • Recent graduates
  • Young professionals
  • Workers
  • Volunteers
  • Entrepreneurs
  • Co-operative members
  • Community organizers
  • People completely new to the co-operative movement

The key requirement is not a particular career status.

Instead, the application is intended to understand:

  • Who you are
  • Why you want to join the Youth Advisory Group
  • What skills you can contribute
  • What experience or perspective you bring

What Co-operatives UK Wants to Know About Applicants

The short application form asks candidates to provide information about:

  1. Who they are
  2. Why they want to become a Youth Advisory Group member
  3. Their skills
  4. Their experience

This means applicants should focus on authenticity rather than trying to present themselves as established experts.

A strong application should clearly communicate:

  • What matters to you
  • Why youth participation matters
  • What perspective you would bring
  • Why you are interested in co-operative ideas
  • How you might contribute to the group

Applications Can Be Written, Video or Audio

Applicants are not limited to traditional written responses.

Co-operatives UK accepts applications through:

  • Written text
  • Video
  • Audio

This can make the process more accessible to applicants who may communicate more effectively through different formats.

Candidates should choose the format that allows them to present their ideas most clearly and authentically.

Written Applications

Candidates who prefer writing can complete the application in text format.

A strong written response should be:

  • Clear
  • Specific
  • Personal
  • Concise
  • Relevant

Applicants do not need to use highly formal corporate language.

The application is designed to understand the person behind the submission.

Video Applications

Young people who communicate more naturally on camera may submit responses through video.

A good video application might explain:

  • Why you want to join
  • What issues matter to you
  • What perspective you can contribute
  • How you would help strengthen youth engagement

Applicants should consult the application form and information pack for any technical requirements concerning video submissions.

Audio Applications

Audio responses are also accepted.

This can be particularly useful for candidates who are comfortable expressing their ideas verbally but do not want to appear on video.

Again, applicants should check the official application materials for format and submission instructions.

How to Apply

Applicants need to:

  1. Download and review the Youth Advisory Group information pack.
  2. Download the official application form.
  3. Complete the application.
  4. Choose written, video, or audio format where appropriate.
  5. Send the completed application to the official email address.

Applications should be sent to: youth@uk.coop

Official Application Resources

Applicants should consult two documents before applying:

Youth Advisory Group Information Pack

The information pack provides additional details about the opportunity and what participation involves.

Official information pack:

https://www.uk.coop/sites/default/files/2026-08/YAG_2026_Information_pack_web.pdf

Youth Advisory Group Application Form

Applicants must complete the official application form.

Application form:

https://www.uk.coop/sites/default/files/2026-08/YAG_Application_Form_2026.pdf

Application Deadline

Applications close at:

23:59 on Sunday, 6 September 2026.

Applicants should send their submissions before the deadline.

Because applications may involve video or audio files, candidates using those formats should avoid waiting until the final minutes in case they encounter:

  • File-size problems
  • Upload difficulties
  • Email issues
  • Technical delays

Why Young People Should Consider Applying

The Youth Advisory Group offers a relatively unusual opportunity for young people to contribute directly to the strategic thinking of an established national organization.

Participants can potentially gain experience in:

  • Advisory work
  • Youth advocacy
  • Strategic discussion
  • Collaboration
  • Public engagement
  • Co-operative development
  • Leadership
  • Community engagement
  • Social and economic policy conversations

Unlike programmes that focus primarily on training participants, this opportunity asks young people to contribute their existing experiences and perspectives to real organizational discussions.

Opportunity to Influence an Established Movement

The co-operative movement includes organizations operating across many sectors of society and the economy.

Young people participating in the YAG can contribute to discussions about how the movement evolves and responds to changing expectations.

This could be particularly valuable for candidates interested in questions such as:

  • What should ethical business look like?
  • How can workers have more influence?
  • How can communities own local assets?
  • How should organizations respond to climate change?
  • How can young people participate more meaningfully in economic decision-making?
  • What alternatives exist to traditional business ownership?

Applicants do not need to arrive with answers to these questions.

A willingness to engage with them can itself be valuable.

Skills Participants May Develop

Although the supplied call does not present a formal training curriculum, participation could help members strengthen transferable skills through practical involvement.

These may include:

  • Communication
  • Teamwork
  • Strategic thinking
  • Advocacy
  • Public speaking
  • Collaboration
  • Idea development
  • Constructive challenge
  • Community engagement
  • Stakeholder engagement

Members may also develop a stronger understanding of how organizational decision-making and youth participation operate in practice.

Building Networks

The Youth Advisory Group brings together young people from:

  • Existing co-operatives
  • The wider co-operative movement
  • Different youth networks
  • Backgrounds outside co-operatives

This creates opportunities for participants to meet peers with different experiences and perspectives.

For young people interested in:

  • Social enterprise
  • Co-operatives
  • Sustainability
  • Community development
  • Youth leadership
  • Alternative business models

the group may provide useful professional and personal connections.

Preparing a Strong Application

1. Explain Why the Opportunity Matters to You

Avoid giving a generic response such as:

“I want to develop my leadership skills.”

Instead, explain what specific issue motivates you.

Perhaps you care about:

  • Climate action
  • Fair employment
  • Communities
  • Ethical business
  • Youth voice
  • Economic inequality

Connect that interest with why the YAG appeals to you.

2. You Do Not Need to Pretend to Be a Co-operative Expert

The call explicitly welcomes applicants who are completely new to co-operatives.

If you are unfamiliar with the movement, say so honestly.

You could instead explain:

  • Why you want to learn
  • What perspective you bring from outside the movement
  • What issues already matter to you

Being new to co-operatives is not presented as a disadvantage.

3. Give Concrete Examples

When discussing your skills, use examples.

Instead of saying:

“I am a good communicator,”

you might explain how you:

  • Organized a student project
  • Spoke at a community event
  • Ran social media for a group
  • Volunteered with young people
  • Participated in a campaign
  • Helped resolve a disagreement

Evidence makes an application stronger.

4. Explain What Young People Need

The YAG exists partly to make Co-operatives UK more responsive to younger generations.

Think about:

  • What young people currently worry about
  • What opportunities they need
  • Why traditional institutions may not engage them
  • How co-operatives could become more relevant

Your perspective does not need to match everyone else’s.

The purpose of an advisory group is partly to hear different views.

5. Choose the Best Application Format for You

You can apply using:

  • Writing
  • Video
  • Audio

Do not automatically choose written text because it seems more formal.

Use whichever format lets you communicate most effectively.

Important Details at a Glance

Organization: Co-operatives UK

Programme: Youth Advisory Group

Abbreviation: YAG

Established: 2024

Applicant age: 16–30

Previous co-operative experience: Not required

Experience level: All levels welcome

Payment: Members are paid for their time

Application formats: Written, video, or audio

Application email: youth@uk.coop

Deadline: 6 September 2026 at 23:59

Information: https://www.uk.coop/news/applications-now-open-co-operatives-uks-youth-advisory-group

Conclusion

The Co-operatives UK Youth Advisory Group 2026 offers young people aged 16 to 30 an opportunity to have a meaningful voice in discussions about the future of the co-operative movement.

Established in 2024, the group works alongside Co-operatives UK to provide strategic advice, generate new ideas, challenge existing thinking, advocate for youth participation, and increase awareness of co-operative approaches among younger generations.

The opportunity is deliberately accessible. Applicants do not need previous co-operative experience, a university degree, a particular profession, or extensive leadership credentials. Young people with all levels of skills and experience are encouraged to apply.

The group may be particularly relevant to young people interested in fairness, climate action, community development, youth participation, sustainability, or alternative approaches to business and ownership.

Importantly, Youth Advisory Group members are paid for their time, recognizing both their contribution and the commitment involved.

Applications can be submitted in written, video, or audio format, allowing candidates to choose the communication method that works best for them.

Applicants must complete the official application form and send it to youth@uk.coop.

The application deadline is 23:59 on Sunday, 6 September 2026.

 

To learn more about this opportunity, VISIT HERE.

 

To explore more global opportunities, CLICK HERE.

item.content:encoded:
The Second UNCTAD Supply Chain Innovation Challenge 2026 is now accepting proposals from innovators around the world with ideas for using frontier technologies to build more sustainable, resilient, efficient and inclusive global supply chains.

Organized as an integral part of the Second United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD) Global Supply Chain Forum (GSCF), the challenge provides individuals and teams with an international platform to propose practical and innovative solutions to some of the most pressing disruptions affecting supply chains worldwide.

The UNCTAD Global Supply Chain Forum 2026 will take place in Riyadh, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, from 29 November to 1 December 2026.

Building on the inaugural Supply Chain Innovation Challenge held during the first Global Supply Chain Forum in Barbados in 2024, the second edition seeks original proposals demonstrating how frontier technologies can help countries, businesses and communities anticipate, withstand and recover from current and emerging supply chain disruptions.

The winning proposal will be presented at the Second UNCTAD Global Supply Chain Forum in Saudi Arabia, with travel and accommodation expenses covered.

The deadline to submit a proposal is 4 September 2026 at 23:59 (GMT+2).

About the UNCTAD Supply Chain Innovation Challenge 2026

Global supply chains are essential to international trade, food security, economic development and the movement of goods and services around the world. However, recent years have demonstrated how vulnerable supply networks can be to unexpected shocks and long-term structural challenges.

The Second UNCTAD Supply Chain Innovation Challenge seeks ideas capable of responding to these challenges through technology-driven innovation.

This year’s challenge focuses specifically on the potential of frontier technologies to improve the ability of supply chains to anticipate disruption, withstand shocks and recover effectively.

Successful proposals should consider how technological innovation can contribute to supply chains that are:

  • More sustainable;
  • More resilient;
  • More efficient;
  • More inclusive;
  • Better prepared for future disruptions; and
  • Practically applicable in real-world supply chain environments.

Rather than focusing only on theoretical concepts, UNCTAD is looking for proposals that demonstrate how innovative ideas could work in practice and create meaningful improvements across supply chains.

What Is the UNCTAD Global Supply Chain Forum?

The Global Supply Chain Forum is an international UNCTAD platform focused on the challenges, opportunities and transformations shaping global supply chains.

The second edition of the forum will be held in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, from 29 November to 1 December 2026.

The 2026 Supply Chain Innovation Challenge forms an integral part of this international forum, giving innovators an opportunity to contribute practical solutions to the broader global discussion surrounding resilient and sustainable supply chains.

The challenge follows the success of the first Supply Chain Innovation Challenge held during the inaugural Global Supply Chain Forum in Barbados in 2024.

The winning proposal from the 2026 challenge will have the opportunity to reach an international audience through presentation at the forum.

Focus of the Second Supply Chain Innovation Challenge

The central focus of the challenge is:

How can frontier technologies help anticipate, withstand and recover from global supply chain disruptions while making supply chains more sustainable, resilient, efficient and inclusive?

Applicants are encouraged to think beyond conventional approaches and demonstrate how emerging and frontier technologies could address existing problems or prepare supply chains for challenges likely to emerge in the coming years.

Proposals should combine innovation with practical implementation.

UNCTAD particularly emphasizes solutions that demonstrate a commitment to:

  • Sustainability;
  • Inclusivity;
  • Resilience;
  • Practical applicability; and
  • Real-world impact.

Priority Areas for Proposals

Applicants are welcome to propose solutions addressing a wide range of supply chain challenges.

However, UNCTAD particularly encourages proposals addressing the following areas.

1. Making Supply Chains Greener

Applicants may explore how frontier technologies can reduce the environmental impact of supply chains and contribute to more sustainable trade and logistics systems.

Solutions could consider challenges associated with transportation, logistics, resource efficiency, environmental monitoring or other aspects of sustainable supply chain management.

The fundamental objective should be to demonstrate how innovation can contribute to greener supply chains while remaining practical and scalable.

2. Ensuring Food Security Through Resilient Supply Chains

Food supply chains can be particularly vulnerable to disruptions, making resilience critical to ensuring that food reaches communities reliably and efficiently.

Applicants may propose innovative technological solutions capable of strengthening food-related supply chains, improving their resilience or helping stakeholders anticipate and respond to disruptions.

Solutions should demonstrate how technology can contribute to reliable, resilient and sustainable supply systems.

3. Streamlining Cross-Border Procedures in Supply Chains

International supply chains frequently involve multiple jurisdictions, procedures and stakeholders.

The challenge therefore encourages solutions that explore how frontier technologies can make cross-border supply chain processes more efficient and resilient.

Applicants may consider innovative approaches that improve processes associated with international movement, coordination or supply chain management.

Importantly, applicants are not restricted to these three areas.

Innovative proposals addressing other relevant supply chain disruptions are also eligible, provided they align with the overall objectives of the challenge.

What Applicants Must Submit

Participants must submit an original proposal written in English.

The proposal should be between 1,500 and 3,000 words maximum, including the bibliography and footnotes.

Applicants should ensure their submission clearly explains both the challenge they are addressing and how their proposed technological solution could address it.

UNCTAD specifies four core components that should be included.

1. A Clear Problem Statement

Applicants should begin by clearly identifying the supply chain problem or disruption they intend to address.

The problem statement should provide enough context to explain:

  • What the problem is;
  • Why it matters;
  • Who or what is affected;
  • How it affects supply chain resilience, efficiency, sustainability or inclusion; and
  • Why an innovative solution is needed.

A well-defined problem statement provides the foundation for the remainder of the proposal.

2. Detailed Description of the Innovative Solution

Applicants must explain the solution they are proposing.

The proposal should demonstrate how frontier technology can be applied to prepare for, counter or respond to supply chain disruptions.

The description should be sufficiently detailed to allow evaluators to understand how the proposed solution would work and what makes it innovative.

3. Anticipated Impact

Applicants should explain the expected impact of their solution.

The proposal should demonstrate how the innovation could contribute to stronger supply chains and what improvements could reasonably result from its implementation.

Applicants should consider the broader objectives of creating supply chains that are sustainable, inclusive, resilient and effective in real-world environments.

4. Feasibility Assessment

Innovation alone is not enough. Applicants must also demonstrate that their proposed solution has practical applicability.

The feasibility assessment should explain why and how the idea could realistically be implemented.

This is particularly important because feasibility is one of the official criteria that will be used to assess proposals.

Proposal Length and Language Requirements

Applicants should carefully follow the submission requirements.

The proposal must:

  • Be an original submission;
  • Be written in English;
  • Contain between 1,500 and 3,000 words maximum;
  • Include the bibliography and footnotes within the stated word limit;
  • Present a clear supply chain problem;
  • Explain an innovative frontier technology solution;
  • Discuss anticipated impact; and
  • Demonstrate practical feasibility.

Applicants should review their final submission carefully before submitting it to ensure it complies with these requirements.

Who Can Apply for the UNCTAD Supply Chain Innovation Challenge?

The challenge is open to natural persons, meaning individual people rather than organizations or legal entities.

Applicants may participate individually or form a team.

Teams may consist of up to four people.

If a team is selected as the winner, one member of the team will represent the group in Saudi Arabia.

This is an important consideration for teams preparing their applications, particularly when deciding who may be available to participate in the Global Supply Chain Forum if selected.

International Eligibility

The call invites innovators from around the world to propose solutions.

The information provided for the challenge does not specify a particular nationality, region or continent to which applicants must belong.

This gives the competition an international scope and allows innovators from different backgrounds and geographic regions to contribute ideas addressing global supply chain challenges.

Applicants should nevertheless carefully review the official application form and any associated terms before submission for any additional requirements.

Evaluation Criteria

Proposals submitted to the Second UNCTAD Supply Chain Innovation Challenge will be assessed according to five major criteria:

Innovation

Evaluators will consider the originality and innovative qualities of the proposed solution.

Applicants should demonstrate what makes their idea distinctive and how frontier technology provides a meaningful approach to the supply chain challenge identified.

Feasibility

Proposals should demonstrate that the solution can realistically be implemented.

A highly innovative concept should therefore be accompanied by a credible explanation of how it could work in practice.

Scalability

Evaluators will consider the potential for the proposed solution to expand or be applied more broadly.

Applicants should think about whether their innovation could move beyond a limited pilot or local application and potentially address supply chain challenges on a larger scale.

Sustainability

Sustainability is a core theme of the challenge.

Applicants should demonstrate how their proposed solution contributes to sustainable supply chain development and avoids treating sustainability as an afterthought.

Resilience

Proposals should show how the innovation can help supply chains prepare for, withstand or recover from disruption.

Resilience should therefore be integrated into the fundamental design and expected impact of the solution.

What Does the Winner Receive?

One of the most significant opportunities offered through the challenge is the chance for the winning proposal to be presented at the Second UNCTAD Global Supply Chain Forum in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.

The forum will take place from 29 November to 1 December 2026.

For the winning proposal, travel and accommodation expenses will be covered.

For team submissions, only one team member will represent the group in Saudi Arabia if the proposal is selected.

Beyond the covered travel and accommodation, presenting at the Global Supply Chain Forum provides the winner with an international platform for showcasing an innovative solution addressing major global supply chain challenges.

Why Consider Applying?

The UNCTAD Supply Chain Innovation Challenge provides an opportunity for innovators to move their ideas into an international policy and supply chain discussion.

Potential reasons to consider participating include:

  • Presenting an innovative solution on an international platform;
  • Contributing ideas addressing major global supply chain challenges;
  • Exploring the potential of frontier technologies in trade and supply chains;
  • Demonstrating solutions focused on sustainability and resilience;
  • Showcasing an idea at the UNCTAD Global Supply Chain Forum;
  • Engaging with a challenge organized within a United Nations forum; and
  • Receiving covered travel and accommodation if selected to present the winning proposal in Riyadh.

The challenge may be particularly relevant to people working on ideas at the intersection of technology, international trade, logistics, sustainability, food systems, resilience and cross-border processes.

How to Strengthen Your Proposal

Because proposals will be evaluated on innovation, feasibility, scalability, sustainability and resilience, applicants should ensure these qualities are clearly visible throughout their submission.

A strong proposal should not simply describe an interesting technology.

Instead, it should establish a logical connection between:

Supply chain problem → frontier technology solution → practical implementation → measurable impact.

Applicants should clearly explain why their chosen technology is appropriate for the identified problem and why the proposed approach represents an improvement over existing practices.

The feasibility section should also receive significant attention. Applicants should avoid presenting a solution that is technically impressive but difficult to implement in realistic supply chain environments.

Similarly, applicants should consider scalability from the beginning. A solution designed for a particular location or sector may still demonstrate how the underlying approach could potentially be adapted or expanded elsewhere.

Finally, sustainability, inclusivity and resilience should be integrated throughout the proposal rather than addressed only briefly at the end.

Important Dates

Applicants should take note of the following dates:

  • Proposal submission deadline: 4 September 2026 at 23:59 (GMT+2)
  • Second UNCTAD Global Supply Chain Forum: 29 November–1 December 2026
  • Forum location: Riyadh, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia

Applicants are strongly encouraged not to wait until the final hours before submitting their proposals.

Submission Deadline

The official deadline for the Second UNCTAD Supply Chain Innovation Challenge is:

4 September 2026 at 23:59 (GMT+2).

Applications submitted after the deadline may not be considered, so prospective participants should prepare and submit their proposals as early as possible.

Applicants in other time zones should carefully convert the deadline to their local time to avoid missing the submission window.

How to Apply

Interested participants should complete the official application process and submit their proposal through the designated application form.

Before submitting, applicants should ensure that their proposal:

  1. Is original;
  2. Is written in English;
  3. Meets the 1,500–3,000-word requirement, including bibliography and footnotes;
  4. Contains a clear problem statement;
  5. Provides a detailed explanation of the innovative solution;
  6. Explains the anticipated impact;
  7. Includes a feasibility assessment;
  8. Demonstrates sustainability and inclusivity;
  9. Addresses practical application in real-world supply chain settings; and
  10. Is submitted before 4 September 2026 at 23:59 (GMT+2).

Applicants should use the official UNCTAD Supply Chain Innovation Challenge application form to complete their submission.

APPLY NOW

Questions and Further Information

Applicants who have questions about the challenge can contact the organizers at:

gscf@unctad.org

Prospective participants should also consult the official UNCTAD Global Supply Chain Forum information for updates and further details relating to the forum and challenge.

Conclusion

The Second UNCTAD Supply Chain Innovation Challenge 2026 offers innovators worldwide an opportunity to contribute practical technology-driven ideas to one of the most important challenges facing international trade: creating global supply chains capable of anticipating, withstanding and recovering from disruption.

With a strong emphasis on frontier technologies, sustainability, inclusivity, feasibility, scalability and resilience, the challenge is seeking more than theoretical concepts. It is looking for innovative proposals with genuine potential for real-world application.

Individuals can apply independently, while teams of up to four people are also eligible to participate. Applicants must submit an original English-language proposal of between 1,500 and 3,000 words, including bibliography and footnotes.

The winning proposal will be presented at the Second UNCTAD Global Supply Chain Forum in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, from 29 November to 1 December 2026, with travel and accommodation expenses covered.

Innovators with ideas for greener supply chains, resilient food systems, streamlined cross-border procedures or other technology-enabled approaches to global supply chain disruption are encouraged to consider applying.

Applications must be submitted by 4 September 2026 at 23:59 (GMT+2).

Visit the OFY website for more opportunities on global competitions.

item.content:encoded:
Applications are open for two funded PhD scholarship opportunities at the University of Cape Town (UCT) for 2027, offered through the Desmond Tutu HIV Centre and the Desmond Tutu Health Foundation (DTHF) in collaboration with the University of Cape Town in South Africa.

The scholarships are designed for research-ready candidates who want to pursue rigorous doctoral research while contributing to established and actively funded global health research programmes. Successful candidates will undertake their PhDs through the UCT Department of Medicine and will work within multidisciplinary research environments emphasizing publication, analytical skills, academic development, mentorship, and increasing research independence.

Each successful candidate will receive funding valued at:

R315,000 per year

The scholarship provides core funding for the first three years of the PhD. A fourth year may be supported, but this additional year is conditional on satisfactory academic progress, including evidence of manuscript development and progress with thesis completion. The scholarship contributes toward tuition and living costs and must be held together with formal PhD registration at the University of Cape Town.

The opportunity is restricted geographically: applicants must be South African citizens or permanent residents of South Africa. Preparing a Competitive Application

1. Demonstrate Research Readiness

This opportunity is explicitly aimed at research-ready candidates.

Use your CV, research concept, PhD plan, and writing sample collectively to demonstrate that you already understand how research is developed and conducted.

2. Make Your Methodological Skills Visible

Qualitative, quantitative, or mixed-methods experience is a formal requirement.

State clearly:

  • Which methods you used
  • What data you analyzed
  • Which analytical tools you know
  • What outputs resulted

A one-page research concept cannot support an overly broad project.

Instead of proposing something such as:

“Improving HIV prevention in South Africa,”

a stronger concept would identify:

  • A specific population
  • A particular intervention
  • A defined knowledge gap
  • A researchable outcome

The exact project should be tailored to the research environment and applicant’s expertise.

4. Show Publication Potential

Because the programme is explicitly publication-oriented, explain how the project could produce several coherent manuscripts or academic outputs.

Your three-year plan should reinforce this.

5. Choose the Writing Sample Carefully

The writing sample is being used as evidence of your:

  • Academic writing
  • Analytical ability
  • Conceptual thinking

Choose your strongest relevant piece rather than simply the most recent document available.

6. Demonstrate Long-Term Research Motivation

The programme is intended to prepare researchers for postdoctoral or research-intensive career pathways.

Applicants should therefore explain how the PhD fits within their longer-term academic or research trajectory.
